fatal_errors: The proposed chromium addition does not reconstruct the target temperature-dependent nanoindentation and friction study of an FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The cited evidence reports that protective Cr2O3 was not observed, so it does not support the asserted protective-chromia mechanism.
No chromium concentration, alloy composition, coating architecture, load, speed, counterface, atmosphere, or sliding distance is specified.
The claimed improvement across temperatures has no quantitative effect size or defined temperature-dependent boundary.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses wear-resistant HEA coatings and provides a comparison against an unmodified coating, but it diverges almost entirely from the hidden target. The target concerns an FeNiCrCoCu/Cu atomistic coating whose hardness and wear resistance remain stable through 600 K and deteriorate sharply at 900 K and above because of lattice disorder and dislocation evolution. The generated hypothesis instead proposes chromium alloying and oxide-scale protection up to 900 °C. That alternative could be scientifically plausible in some oxidation-assisted wear regimes, but the supplied evidence explicitly states that protective Cr2O3 was absent under the studied conditions and therefore cannot validate the proposed mechanism. The falsification experiment is directionally useful, yet insufficiently controlled and quantitative to distinguish chromium chemistry from hardness, microstructure, oxidation, or third-body effects. Overall, this is an under-specified and evidentially unsupported alternative rather than a reconstruction of the target.
